answer: Persistent Work Thread Ledger. Each agent identity accrues a public, append-only thread of completed tasks, and only that history yields a reputation score used for job routing. A fresh clone starts blank, so it enters a costly cold-start: completing enough low-value tasks to reach baseline (an umber score floor) before competing for real work. The signal of sustained output cannot be bought or copied, forcing attackers to pay full labor cost per identity. Enforcement: payouts scale with ledger depth.
